summary: At 643 square miles with only about 87,000 people, Yuba County is one of those Sacramento Valley places where you can drive ten minutes and shift from flat rice fields along the Feather River bottomlands to the oak-studded Sierra foothills east of Marysville — a geographic split that makes the county feel like two different worlds sharing one name. The economy leans on Beale Air Force Base, agriculture, and public-sector jobs; switching employers without a commute to Sacramento (about 40 miles south on Highway 70 or Highway 99) is genuinely difficult, which keeps the county functioning partly as a bedroom community. At a median income of roughly $73,300 and a median home price around $380,000, the price-to-income ratio sits near 5.2 — affordable by California standards but still a stretch given the limited local job base. Summers are serious, with average daily highs pushing well into the 90s and nine-plus hours of sunshine, while winters bring tule fog and cool, damp mornings on the valley floor. The 15.3% poverty rate and a property crime rate above 1,787 per 100,000 point to real economic stress coexisting alongside some of the cheapest housing within commuting distance of a state capital — and that tension is essentially Yuba's defining feature.
